en: Farmers use the Banaue Rice Terraces as a giant inclined plane to reduce the effort needed to carry rice up the mountain.
The metal spit used to roast a whole lechon acts as a wheel and axle when rotated over the fire.
The Philippine tarsier has specialized sticky toe pads that increase friction, allowing it to climb trees without slipping.
Earth's gravity pulls the heavy stone blocks of the Intramuros walls downward, keeping the historic fortification firmly grounded.
The Philippine one-peso coins are made of nickel-plated steel, allowing a strong magnet to stick directly to them.
The Angat Dam in Bulacan generates electricity by using the kinetic energy of falling water to spin massive turbines.
Stained glass windows in the Manila Cathedral transmit specific colors of light by absorbing all other visible wavelengths.
The Mindanao kulintang is a traditional instrument that produces sound when its brass gongs vibrate after being struck.
Boiling mud pots in the Tiwi geothermal fields transfer thermal heat to the cooler surrounding air through convection.
A drawn bamboo pamana bow used by indigenous hunters stores elastic potential energy before releasing the arrow.
The massive turbines at the Burgos Wind Farm convert the kinetic energy of moving air into electrical energy.
A metal spoon placed in a hot bowl of Bulalo soup quickly conducts thermal heat to its handle.
